 Oral Judgment

(1) Feeling aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 04.02.2022 passed by learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.), Dhoraji at Rajkot, (hereinafter referred to as "the Tribunal" for short), in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.81/2017, the appellant -Insurance Company preferred present appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act" for short).

sentences.text:
(2) Heard Mr. Rathin P. Raval, learned Advocate for the appellant - Insurance Company and Mr.
Nishit Bhalodi, learned counsel for the original claimants.
Though served, none appears for rest of the respondents.

sentences.text: It is the case of the claimants that on 16.08.2017, deceased was going in motorcar bearing No.GJ-03-JL-4952, which was driven by his son Sagar Babubhai Unghad (claimant No.3) and when they reached near Aerodram on Porbandar - Rajkot National Highway, at that time, one another motorcar bearing No.GJ-03-EC-4371 was going ahead of the car of the deceased.
At that time, driver of that car had suddenly applied brakes, due to which, the car of the deceased dashed with it.

As a result, the deceased got serious NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2301/2022 JUDGMENT DATED:
05/02/2026 undefined injuries and succumbed to it.
Therefore, the claim petition was filed by the legal heirs of the deceased to get compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the opponents.
After appreciating the evidence produced on record, the learned Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.16,02,000/- along with cost and interest @ 9 % p.a.

( 4 ) Learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company has submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in considering the income of the deceased as Rs.15,000/- p.m in absence of any evidence of income and further, in not considering contributory negligence on the part of the deceased.
Therefore, at least 50 % contributed negligence ought to have been held by the Tribunal on the part of the deceased.
On the aforesaid grounds, learned counsel for the appellant has requested to allow the appeal as prayed for.

(5) Per contra, learned counsel for the original claimants has opposed the present appeal and submitted that the Tribunal has not committed any error in holding sole negligent on the part of the driver of car bearing No.GJ-03-EC-4371 because the accident occurred only because of negligence on his part.
Further, no any evidence is produced on record to rebut or presume that the deceased was negligent in causing the accident.
The Tribunal has properly relied on the authorities delivered in case of National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Chamundeshwari Devi, reported in (2021) 9 SCC 439.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Chamundeshwari Devi, reported in (2021) 9 SCC 439
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He has also submitted that, the Tribunal considering the fact that the deceased was owner of the car and from one day, he owned lath machine, considered his income as Rs.15,000/- p.m.
Hence, no error has been committed by the Tribunal.
Even deceased was driving the car as an occupant and hence, for him, this is a case of composite negligence and therefore, question does not arise to consider contributory negligence.
Further, opponent Nos.1 and 2 did not appear before the Tribunal and have not disputed or rebutted the evidence produced before the Tribunal.

Hence,
question does not arise to consider contributory negligence on the part of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2301/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/02/2026 undefined the deceased.
Hence, he has requested to dismiss the appeal.

(6) Having heard learned counsel for both sides and upon perusal of the material placed on record,
it is evident that the involvement of the offending vehicle and the coverage of the insurance policy are not in dispute.

To substantiate their case, the claimants have produced documentary evidence i.e. FIR at Exh.22, panchnama at Exh.23, post-mortem report at Exh.25, insurance policy of both the drivers at Exhs.28 and 31, driving licence of both the drivers at Exh.26 and 29.
Therefore, the appeal is required to be decided in a narrow compass, qua the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
So far as contributory negligence is concerned, claimant No.1 was eyewitness and has stated that due to sole negligence of the car No.GJ-03-EC-4371, accident occurred.
Nothing has emerged from her cross-examination to establish that the driver of the offending vehicle was not negligent in causing the accident.

The deceased was travelling in the car which was driven by his son and the accident occurred when the offending car was going ahead of The United India Insurance Company ... vs Vilasben Babubhai Undhad on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45387910/
2 their car and due to sudden brakes applied by driver of that car, car of the deceased dashed with that car and deceased lost his life due to severe injuries.
(7) In view of the above, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Tribunal has not committed any error in holding the driver of the car No.GJ- 03-EC4371 solely negligent in causing the accident.
The Tribunal has rightly relied upon the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Bimla Devi v.
HRTC, reported in AIR 2009 SC 2819, and Parmeshwari v. Amir Chand, reported in (2011) 11 SCC 635.
(8)

sentences.text: So far as contributory negligence is concerned, mere allegation that the motorcar bearing No.GJ-03-JL-4952 was negligent is insufficient and amounts to mere lip service.
On the basis of the principle of preponderance of probabilities, the burden lies upon Insurance Company to establish such defence.
Contributory negligence cannot be inferred on presumptions and assumptions.

The standard of proof required is that of preponderance of NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2301/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/02/2026 undefined probabilities, as reiterated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Limited.

entities.text: Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Limited
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reliance is also placed upon the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Srikrishna Kanta Singh v. The Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Ors., reported in 2025 INSC 394.

entities.text: Srikrishna Kanta Singh v. The Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Ors., reported in 2025 INSC 394
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view thereof, the Tribunal has not committed any error in not attributing contributory negligence to the deceased.
Consequently, the argument advanced by learned counsel for the appellant on this count is not sustainable.
(9) Learned counsel for the insurance company, Mr. Raval, has contended that the version of claimant No.1 is contrary to the contents of the FIR.
However, it is pertinent to note that the FIR itself has neither been duly proved nor contents thereof been established in accordance with law.
In any case, the evidence led before the Tribunal is required to be appreciated in light of the principle laid down in Chamundeshwari Devi (supra).

It is further observed that the driver of car bearing No.
GJ-03-EC-4371 neither appeared before the Tribunal nor stepped into the witness box, and has not denied either the involvement of the said vehicle or the negligence of the driver of car bearing No.
GJ-03-JL-4952.

In such circumstances, the Tribunal has rightly relied upon the evidence of the eyewitness and on the basis of the doctrine of preponderance of probabilities, arrived at the conclusion that the accident occurred due to the sudden brakes applied by the driver of car No.
GJ-03-EC-4371.

Moreover, in order to establish contributory negligence on the part of the deceased,
cogent and reliable evidence was required to be produced by opponent Nos.1 and 2 or by the insurance company.
However, no such evidence has been brought on record.
Therefore, the finding recorded by the Tribunal on this aspect does not call for any interference.
(10) So far as the income aspect is concerned, the claimants have pleaded that the deceased was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.

However, no cogent evidence has been produced on record to substantiate the said claim, and the minimum wage prevailing at the time of the accident was Rs.9,000/- per NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2301/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 05/02/2026 undefined month.

However, the Tribunal considering the fact that the deceased was the owner of a car, was running a lathe machine and was maintaining a reasonably good standard of living,
assessed the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.15,000/-.
Therefore, it cannot be said that the Tribunal has committed any error in assessing the income of the deceased at the said amount.

sentences.text: While assessing the income of the deceased, the Tribunal was required to bear in mind the object of the Motor Vehicles Act, which is a beneficial and welfare legislation intended to provide just compensation based on the contemporaneous position of the individual and is essentially forward-looking in nature.
In light of the decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in S. Vishnu Ganga v. M/s.
Oriental
Insurance
Co. Ltd.

, reported in 2025 INSC 123, K. Ramya v. National Insurance Co. Ltd., reported in 2022 SCC OnLine 1338, and Shivleela & Ors. v. The Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co. Ltd., reported in 2025 INSC 357.

sentences.text: (12) So far as addition of 10% towards future prospects is concerned, in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi, reported in 2017 ACJ 2700, and considering that the deceased was aged 55 years, such addition is just and proper.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi, reported in 2017 ACJ 2700
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As the deceased was married and survived by his wife and two sons, deduction of 1/3rd towards personal expenses is in consonance with Sarla Verma (Smt.) & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.,
reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121.

entities.text:
Sarla Verma (Smt.) & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.,
reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The multiplier of 11 has also been correctly applied.
The compensation awarded under other conventional heads are also just and proper.
(13) For the foregoing reasons and observation, no interference is called for in the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
Hence, present appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.
Record and proceedings, if any, be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.
